title: Lesson 11 · The Noun in Depth
blurb: Gender, number & plurals, the four cases, singular vs plural, and noun properties.

Which is the correct plural of “calf”?

items.explain: o after a consonant → oes: hero → heroes.

items.prompt: Which is the correct plural of “goose”?
Which is the correct plural of “ox”?
Which is the correct plural of “mouse”?
Which is the correct plural of “child”?
Which is the correct plural of “brother-in-law”?
items.explain: A compound pluralizes its main word: brothers-in-law.

items.prompt: Which is the correct plural of “sheep”?
items.explain: “sheep” is the same in singular and plural: sheep.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun in ( )?

“Boys skate.” (Boys)

What case is the noun in ( )?

“John’s hat is new.” (John’s)

What case is the noun in ( )?

“Indians hunt buffaloes.” (buffaloes)
items.explain: “buffaloes” is the object of “hunt” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun in ( )?

“James, bring a book.” (James)
items.explain: “James” is used independently, in direct address — absolute case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun in ( )?

“Horses are animals.” (Horses)

What case is the noun in ( )?

“We ran over the bridge.” (bridge)
items.explain: “bridge” is the object of the preposition “over” — objective case.

items.prompt:
What case is the noun in ( )?

“The sun’s rays are warm.” (sun’s)

What case is the noun in ( )?

“Oh, my son!” (son)
items.explain: “son” is used independently, in exclamation — absolute case.

Which case is a subject in?
items.explain: A subject is in the nominative case.

items.prompt: Which case is the object of a verb or preposition in?
items.explain: An object is in the objective case.

items.prompt: Which case shows ownership?
items.explain: Ownership is shown by the possessive case.

items.prompt: How many properties does a noun have (gender, person, number, case)?
items.explain: A noun has four properties: gender, person, number, and case.

items.prompt: What does the property “number” tell?
items.explain: Number tells one (singular) or more than one (plural).

items.prompt: Declension names a noun’s forms for what?
items.explain: Declension names a noun’s forms for number and case.
